_doc: First-person presentation (ADR-0029). Read by the arms generator (tools/assetgen/blender/lib/char_fp.py bakes one fp_* action per hold pose, attack and use) and by ViewModel at runtime. Positions and directions are in camera space (x right, y up, z back; metres). A hand spec places the hand by its grip: 'grip' point, 'dir' (handle axis, thumb side), 'knuckles' (where the knuckles point), 'fist' / 'thumb' curl 0..1 (fist 1 closes round a ~3.5 cm handle, up to 1.3 a bare fist), 'index' extra index curl (-1 points), optional 'curls' {finger: curl} (fingers index, middle, ring, pinky) closing those fingers to their own curl instead of the fist (for the index, instead of fist + index), e.g. a knife held with the little finger off the handle: 'curls': {'ring': 0.9, 'pinky': 0.4}, 'elbow' hint added to the rest elbow direction; or {'on': 'R', 'along': m, 'spin': deg} grips the other hand's handle. Attack and use keys are [frame, channels, ease] with channels relative to the hold: S.move [x,y,z] m, S.rot [pitch, yaw, roll] deg about the camera axes (pivot on the grip), S.elbow, S.along, S.spin and the curls (S.fist, S.thumb, S.index, S.flick, and S.curls {finger: curl}, which overrides those fingers for that key while the rest keep the hold's own; a finger with its own curl at either key eases between what it closes to at each). Edit, then `python tools/build_assets.py --match fp_arms` and import. A hold or an attack/use may set 'fixed_roll': ['R'] (sides) to keep the authored roll of those fists about what they hold (a gun's barrel, an inspect's turn-over); otherwise PoseSolver may roll a fist about its handle to spare the wrist. An attack/use without one inherits its hold's.

wrist._doc: A wrist's range (degrees, ADR-0045): flexion, extension, radial and ulnar deviation (an ellipse between them) and the forearm's roll either way of the thumb-up rest. PoseSolver keeps every baked hand inside it (the elbow swings to line the forearm up first, then the hand turns back about its grip); test_viewmodel_holds checks the baked arms. `comfort` (ADR-0060) is where a wrist rests: the same ellipse, smaller and leaning to extension, and the forearm's roll a hand resting on a table has. A hold at rest (idle, guard, tether) is kept inside it; a strike eases from it to the full range as its hand leaves the hold, a use (`relax`, default 0.5) stays at least half way. A hold hand may be written against its own forearm, `wrist`: [flexion, ulnar deviation, roll] in place of dir/back.

defaults._doc: Hold class of an item without equip.hold: by equip.kind, then (melee) by damage_type, then by category. use_by_category picks the use action for consumables.

bow._doc: Bow (ADR-0057): the bow upright in the left fist, canted top-right and low left of centre, an arrow nocked; the right hand rests on the string at the nock, three fingers hooked. The string and the nocked arrow are not baked: BowRig strings them to the right hand's socket each frame, so they follow any draw. item rot turns the bow's face to the target in the left fist (fixed_roll keeps the solver from spinning the bow about its grip).

bow_drawn._doc: The bow at full draw (its idle loop is the held draw, a slight tremble): bow arm out straight, the string hand anchored under the jaw. Not an item's hold: draw_bow ends here and release_bow starts here.

empty._doc: Bare hands at the lower edge, ready: relaxed, the fingers lightly and evenly curled (the little finger a little further) and lying together, the end joints nearly straight (player report 5: hooked further, they read as crooked claws).

one_hand._doc: Axes, hatchet, machete, hammer: carried low at the right, the head forward and in, edge leading (the knuckles' side); the handle crosses the palm obliquely (item rot: 25 degrees toward the knuckles, as a fist really closes on a haft), so the wrist can drive the head down. The off hand drops below the view.

club._doc: Stone club, steel pipe: both hands on the haft (the left below the right), carried low in front with the head up and in; the haft crosses the right palm obliquely (item rot) so the wrists can bring the head down onto the target.

spear._doc: Spear: low at the right hip, point forward to the centre. The shaft lies diagonally across the rear palm (item rot: 60 degrees about the palm's normal, an oblique grip), so the wrist can hold it forward; the front hand under the shaft follows the shaft, not the socket (ADR-0045).

two_hand._doc: Shovel: carried ready to dig, the rear fist overhand on the butt at the right hip and the shaft running down and forward past the centre, blade low in front; the front hand under the shaft. The shaft lies across the rear palm (item rot: 60 degrees about the palm's normal, an oblique grip as the spear's), so the blade can point down without the wrist bending past its range (TD-172).

light_left._doc: Torch: held up and forward in the left fist low on its shaft, the burning head ahead of the hand at the upper left so it lights the way; the right hand down out of view (it comes up to guard).

flashlight._doc: Flashlight: overhand in the left fist, the lens out of the little-finger side so the beam goes where you look; the forearm crosses the lower left. The right hand down out of view (it comes up to guard).

pistol._doc: Revolver: one-handed low ready in the right fist, barrel forward and a little in, canted a touch so the cylinder shows; the index lies straight along the frame over the trigger guard (on the trigger only to fire). item rot z follows the grip's 15 degree rake so the fist closes along the grip, high under the hammer. The off hand is down out of view; it comes up to reload.

held._doc: Anything small carried on the right palm: resources, medicine, placeables, stones.

stone._doc: A throwing stone low at the right, fingers and thumb wrapped round it, palm in and up a little: ready to draw back and throw (ADR-0057).

molotov._doc: A molotov by the neck in the right fist (how one is thrown), low at the right with the body hanging under the hand and the rag burning just above the knuckles, in view (ADR-0057).

food._doc: A can, a bar, a mushroom: in the right fist, ready to eat.

bottle._doc: A bottle upright in the right fist.

blueprint._doc: Laying out a blueprint: the Field Manual open on the left palm, the right hand pointing.

carry_log._doc: A log on the right shoulder: its front end rises out of the top right; the right hand on its near flank, palm against it and fingers over its top, the left down out of view.

climb._doc: Climbing a ladder's rails (ViewModelClimb): both hands on it at 0.37 m, phase 0 of the hand-over-hand cycle (climb_cycle). No item: what was in hand is stowed while climbing.

climb_rope._doc: Climbing a rope, one hand above the other (ViewModelClimb): both hands on it at 0.37 m, phase 0 of the hand-over-hand cycle (climb_rope_cycle). No item: what was in hand is stowed while climbing.

lighter._doc: Lighter: upright in the left hand in front of the chest, the forearm rising from the lower left, fingers round its body, the thumb's pad down on the wheel (the lighter sits high in the fist, so the thumb rests on it instead of reaching over it: report 5's long, massive thumb) and the flame up and a little forward; the right hand down out of view.

knife._doc: Knives: low at the right in a hammer grip, the point forward and a little up toward the centre, the edge down (an axe's upright carry read wrong on a kitchen knife). Quick forehand slice.

rifle._doc: Bolt-action rifle (ADR-0057): a two-handed long gun at the low ready, the stock in the right shoulder's line, the barrel forward and a touch in. The gun lies in the LEFT fist under the fore-end (hand: L; item rot turns its pointing frame onto the palm, scaled to 0.85 so it fits the arms' reach), so the right hand is free to leave the wrist of the stock and work the bolt; both hands are where the pose solver keeps them (TD-294: the left was authored past its reach and the solver moved it 10 cm, turning the gun so its stock sat by the right ear and the right hand hung 20 cm off it), the right on the stock's wrist; every right-hand key is placed on the gun where the solver puts it at that key, checked in the baked arms with fp_measure.gd. The bolt work stays close to the rest pose (the rifle low across the frame, the left hand on the fore-end in view, the right forearm in from the bottom-right); the bolt handle is bent down (item_firearms BOLT_BEND) so its knob shows clear of the scope's ocular bell on screen (fp_measure FP_READ). No tether reading with it up (both hands busy). aim: the scope's ocular (socket_sight) comes up onto the line of sight 7 cm before the eye; the scope picture takes over from there.

attacks._doc: fp_<name>: played over the item's attack_time, so `impact` (the hit resolves at attack_time x impact) sits on the keyed contact frame.

draw_bow._doc: Draw (attack held; frozen at the draw fraction by BowHandler, so a let-down plays it backwards): the bow comes up and out while the string hand starts back, then the long pull to the anchor under the jaw. Mid-draw the string hand passes low and to the right of the bow's grip, not over it (TD-291: it covered the grip from the view).

release_bow._doc: Release (attack let go past min_draw): the fingers open, the string hand flies back past the jaw and the bow arm follows through; then the right hand comes forward to nock the next arrow and the bow settles back to the ready.

throw_stone._doc: Overhand stone throw: drawn back beside the head (held there while the throw charges, `windup`), whipped forward, the fingers opening at `release`.

throw_molotov._doc: Overhand molotov throw: drawn back high by the shoulder (`windup`, held while charging), the bottle lobbed forward and let go at `release`.

light_molotov._doc: Lighting the rag: the left hand comes up cupped round the neck, the thumb flicks a lighter, and drops away again; the bottle tips toward it.

climb_cycle._doc: Hand over hand on a ladder's rails: each hand grips for 70% of the cycle, riding down with the climb (so it stays on the rail), then lets go and reaches up. Not played: ViewModelClimb seeks it to the phase the distance climbed gives (viewmodel.json climb.cycle_m).

climb_grab._doc: Grab-on: the hands come up from below the view and close on it.

climb_release._doc: Let-go (off the top, off the foot or Jump): the hands open and drop out of the view.

climb_rope_cycle._doc: Hand over hand on a rope, one hand above the other: each hand grips for 70% of the cycle, riding down with the climb (so it stays on the rail), then lets go and reaches up. Not played: ViewModelClimb seeks it to the phase the distance climbed gives (viewmodel.json climb.cycle_m).

climb_rope_grab._doc: Grab-on: the hands come up from below the view and close on it.

climb_rope_release._doc: Let-go (off the top, off the foot or Jump): the hands open and drop out of the view.

fire_pistol._doc: A shot: on top of the procedural recoil, the muzzle flips and the wrist soaks it up, back on aim in a quarter second; the index on the trigger, then back along the frame.

reload_pistol._doc: Reload (played over equip.reload_time): the gun comes in and rolls left, the off hand comes up under it, the cylinder swings out (parts: the revolver's `cylinder` node about its crane, deg, keyed in frames), muzzle up and a slap on the ejector rod, muzzle down, the thumb presses three pairs of rounds home, the cylinder snaps shut and the gun goes back to the ready.

inspect_pistol._doc: Look it over (Y): the revolver comes in and turns to show its right side, then rolls over to show the left and the cylinder, and goes back to the ready.

fire_rifle._doc: A shot and the bolt (played over equip.attack_time + bolt_time): the rifle bucks up and back into the shoulder, then comes down a little and turns its right side to the eye (the action low in the frame's right half, the bent-down knob clear of the scope) while the right hand, its forearm in from the bottom-right, goes from the wrist to the bolt knob: up, back (the empty flies), forward, down, and back to the wrist. parts: the rifle's `bolt` node, turned about the bore (deg) and slid along it (m).

reload_rifle_open._doc: Reload, first: the rifle comes down a little, its right side to the eye, the action in view, the right hand lifts the bolt and draws it back (equip.reload_open_time).

reload_rifle._doc: Reload, each round (equip.reload_time, repeated up to the magazine): the right hand drops for a round, brings it over the open action and thumbs it down, back to the bolt knob. The bolt stays open (parts).

reload_rifle_close._doc: Reload, last: the bolt runs forward and turns down, the right hand goes back to the wrist and the rifle to the ready (equip.reload_close_time).

inspect_rifle._doc: Look it over (Y): the rifle comes up and in, rolls onto its left side to show the bolt and the scope's turrets, then tips the muzzle up and across to look along the top and the left of the stock, and back to the ready; the right hand stays on the wrist.

tether._doc: Raising the left wrist to read the tether (T): the reading pose, how long the raise and lower take, the viewmodel's narrower field of view while reading (the screen fills more of the view), and the screen's glow lowered / raised.

guard._doc: Holding Block with a melee weapon raises the hold's guard: a blow from within arc_deg of where you face loses the hold's (or equip.block's) share of its damage, costing stamina per blocked hit plus per point absorbed. You can't attack while guarding.

aim._doc: Aiming a gun (right mouse, ADR-0057): seconds to raise it (time), the view's magnification when up (zoom), multipliers on spread, the arms' sway and walking speed when up, and from what fraction of the raise a scoped gun shows its scope picture. Per item, equip.aim overrides these (the rifle's 4x scope, the revolver's iron sights); where the gun sits when up is its hold's `aim` (the sight socket, its height above it, how far before the eye, the arms' field of view).

motion._doc: Procedural motion on top of the baked poses. breathe: period s, pos m, rot deg. sway: the rig lags the view (deg of lag per rad/s of turn), sprung. move: lag against velocity changes. bob: per footstep (pos m, rot deg), scaled when sprinting / crouched. sprint: the lowered pose (pos m, rot deg) blended in while sprinting. land: dip per m/s of landing speed. equip: seconds to raise a new item. rest (ADR-0060): empty hands standing still for `delay` s sink by pos (m) / rot (deg), at `sink` (per s, eased) and come back at `wake`.

impact._doc: Feedback when a swing connects, by what it hit: hitstop (s the swing freezes), camera kick (pitch, yaw, roll deg; sprung back), rig recoil (m), and particles where the target makes none of its own.

stagger._doc: Taking a hit knocks the arms: deg and m per point of damage, capped; a blocked hit jolts the guard instead.

climb._doc: Climbing arms (ViewModelClimb, ADR-0057): the hand-over-hand cycle advances by the metres climbed over cycle_m (a gripping hand rides down 0.89 m of view per metre climbed at the hold's depth, so it stays on the rail), backwards climbing down, still holding on. grab_time / release_time: seconds of the grab-on and let-go. anchor: the arms stay level and square to the ladder, not the view (1 = fully). bake_fov: the world FOV the climb poses were baked for; at another FOV the rig is scaled across the screen by tan(bake/2)/tan(fov/2) so the hands stay on the rails (TD-296).

_doc_off_hand: Holds that use one hand drop the other below the view (it comes up to guard or read the tether): the owner's playtest found an open hand floating palm-down in the lower corner distracting.

offhand._doc: Items shown for a moment in the other hand (ViewModel.show_offhand): pos (m) and rot (deg) in that hand's socket. The lighter that lights a molotov's rag (TD-291).
